context.text: When a patient sees doctors at several different clinics, their combined record often contains duplicate prescriptions under different brand names, conflicting kidney-disease stages, or outdated medications. We tested four AI setups on 32 clinical questions: a single model reading the condensed chart alone, a single model with automated clinical rules attached, a two-model writer-and-reviewer pair, and a four-agent specialist team. A single AI model reading the chart on its own passed only 17 of 32 questions (80.0/100) because it overlooked brand-vs-generic drug duplicates and age-specific vaccine rules. Attaching automated clinical rule alerts raised the pass rate to 24/32 (80.7/100), adding a second reviewer model reached 29/32 (83.1/100), and the four-agent specialist team passed all 32 questions (88.6/100) while writing in clearer, more patient-friendly language.
